subject: Creative output clauses and legal staging
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@creativeco.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Creative output clauses and legal staging

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached is our initial Order Form and a short redline set from our procurement team (attached as CreativeCo_OrderForm_v1.pdf). Legal has flagged three areas we need clarified before we can move to signature:

1) Output ownership: CreativeCo needs confirmation that content produced by the service using our prompts will be assigned to us (or that Redwood will provide an assignment clause).
2) Training & feedback: We want explicit opt-out for model retraining on our data and a granular telemetry/feedback license that allows productization only with consent.
3) Evidence for compliance: list of artifacts Redwood can provide (audit logs, telemetry tagging, retention policies).

Can you confirm your standard position and whether there are limited commercial options (e.g., paid add-on for assignment or evidence package)? If helpful, I can loop in our counsel on a follow-up two-way redline doc.

Attachments: CreativeCo_OrderForm_v1.pdf

Best,
Elena Park
Head of Partnerships, CreativeCo
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@creativeco.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Creative output clauses and legal staging

Hi Elena — thanks for the doc and the clear summary. Happy to align and propose a narrow path forward so procurement can hit its timeline. High-level answers up front, then an action plan:

- Output ownership: Redwood typically licenses outputs to customers and does not claim ownership of customer content. Assignment is uncommon, but we can offer a limited assignment for specific productization scenarios as a negotiated term in the Order Form (this would be tied to pricing/commitments).

- Training & feedback: Our default is a feedback license that allows use of telemetry to improve service quality but excludes customer content from model retraining unless the customer opts in. We can add explicit opt-out language and a telemetry tagging requirement (we will honor a "do-not-train" flag on calls).

- Evidence: We can provide a standard evidence bundle (audit log export, retention policy summary, telemetry tag report) as a paid compliance add-on or for customers on Dedicated/Private tiers.

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
1) Ben to produce redline of Article 5 (IP) + Section on Feedback License by Tue 5/4. (Ben: see attached draft Exhibit A that sketches assignment language and do-not-train flag.)
2) CreativeCo to confirm whether you require assignment broadly or only for specific downstream product features (reply by 5/4 EOD).
3) Laura and I will map procurement timeline and escalation path if legal needs executive sign-off.

Attachments: redwood-ip-exhibitA-draft.docx

If you agree, we can do a short legal-to-legal call on Wednesday to walk through the redlines.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena@creativeco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Creative output clauses and legal staging

Elena / Monica — attaching a tracked redline for Article 5 and a short cover note. Summary of my recommendations:

- Output: We propose a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive license to use Customer Output, with an optional assignment clause limited to the specific SKU(s) where CreativeCo pays an assignment premium. This prevents unintended transfer of third-party rights while giving negotiating flexibility.

- Training: Add explicit clause: "Customer data and Customer Output will not be used to train base models or create derivatives for use outside the Customer's tenancy unless Customer provides express written consent." Also: require a per-request header or parameter ("x-redwood-dnt") to mark data as "do-not-train."

- Feedback license: Narrow the license to operational use (improve service quality, bug fixes, telemetry) and exclude commercial productization without separate written agreement. Include retention maximums and an evidence export SLA (48-72 hours for audit log export on request).

Open items for commercial: whether assignment is limited to Deployable Products vs. full assignment; suggested commercial metric is TCV banding (assignment allowed above $X TCV).

Attachments: redlines-tracked.docx

On Wed at 10:00 PT I can join a legal-to-legal call if useful. Laura — can you confirm if procurement needs a PO milestone tied to assignment approval?

—Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena@creativeco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, CreativeCo Legal <legal@creativeco.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Creative output clauses and legal staging

Thanks Ben — the redlines look reasonable and the do-not-train header approach should work for our engineering team. A couple of quick clarifications before we lock dates:

- Assignment scope: we only need assignment for outputs that CreativeCo will ship as part of our flagship product (Deployable Products). TCV threshold is fine; we will propose a band and send back a short note.
- Evidence SLA: 72 hours is acceptable. Can you include an internal contact for audit exports so our security team knows whom to ping?

We are good to schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call tomorrow at 10:00 PT. Once we align, procurement will aim to sign within 7 business days.

Elena Park
Head of Partnerships, CreativeCo
CreativeCo Legal (cc'd)
